title: CBT Explained: How Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Actually Works
description: A clear explanation of CBT - the most researched therapy type. How it works, what sessions look like, who it helps, and how it compares to other approaches.

content.text: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) is the most studied psychotherapy in existence. It's the gold standard for depression, anxiety, and many other conditions. Here's how it actually works.
The Core Idea
CBT is based on a simple but powerful insight: our thoughts, feelings, and behaviors are all connected. Change one, and you can change the others.
It's not events that upset us, but our interpretation of them.
When you're depressed or anxious, your thinking becomes distorted. You catastrophize, mind-read, overgeneralize. CBT teaches you to catch these distortions and correct them.
How CBT Works
Identify Automatic Thoughts
You learn to notice the thoughts that pop up automatically in response to situations. 'My boss didn't say hi—she must hate my work.'
Examine the Evidence
You evaluate whether these thoughts are accurate. What's the actual evidence? What would you tell a friend thinking this?
Develop Balanced Thoughts
You create more realistic alternatives. 'My boss seemed distracted. It probably has nothing to do with me.'
Behavioral Experiments
You test your beliefs through action. Avoiding situations maintains anxiety—gradually facing them breaks the cycle.
What Sessions Look Like

items: Homework between sessions (thought records, behavioral tasks)
Collaborative—you and therapist work as a team
Focus on present problems, not childhood

content.text: What CBT Treats Best
Meta-analyses show CBT is highly effective for depression (d=0.73), generalized anxiety (d=0.80), panic disorder (d=0.91), and social anxiety (d=0.86).
content.citation: Hofmann et al., Cognitive Therapy and Research, 2012

content.text: CBT vs. Other Therapies
CBT vs. Psychodynamic
CBT is structured, short-term, focused on present. Psychodynamic is exploratory, often longer, focused on unconscious patterns and past.
CBT vs. DBT
DBT is a type of CBT plus mindfulness and emotional regulation. Originally for borderline personality disorder, now used for emotion dysregulation broadly.
The Bottom Line

CBT works. It's backed by hundreds of studies and helps most people with depression and anxiety. It's practical, time-limited, and teaches skills you keep forever. If you're not sure what therapy to try, CBT is a solid first choice.
